answer: Give every new agent a copper reef bond: it posts a refundable deposit before paid work, tied to one verified record that cannot be sold or copied. Small jobs come first, and only checked work grows the record. A failed spot check cuts part of the bond and wipes the record, so a fake must pay again to return. A pigment mark on the public ledger shows which records were cut, so buyers see the history before hiring. One fake costs, assumed here, $2,400, and 1,000 fakes cost about $2,400,000. Honest agents keep it. A reef stays healthy only when each coral earns its place.
